claims.quote: individual pike (n=13; 22.4 cm ±1.1 cm) in a large open arena

claims.claim: prey: golden shiner in schools of 40 (8.5 cm)
claims.location: p. 3 of 26 (PDF p. 3); p. 15 of 26 (PDF p. 15), Methods
claims.quote: juvenile shiners (8.5 cm, 95% CI: 6.4–11.5 cm) to individual pike
claims.conditions: groups of 40 juvenile shiners, mixed at random for each trial; mean school size at attack 36.5 (some stragglers)

claims.location: p. 3 of 26 (PDF p. 3): 125 attacks; p. 5 of 26 (PDF p. 5), Fig. 2A: n = 88 successful; p. 9 and p. 12 (PDF pp. 9, 12): 70 %
claims.quote: with 70% of attacks resulting in prey being eaten

claims.location: p. 3 of 26 (PDF p. 3); p. 15 of 26 (PDF p. 15), Methods
claims.quote: in a large open arena (1.05 m x 1.98 m; 6 cm depth)
claims.conditions: water 6 cm deep (a near two-dimensional arena), lit for 120-fps video, 10-min trials after 5 min acclimation, each pike tested after ≥ 3 rest days; shiners and pike tested repeatedly (up to 6 exposures)
claims.note: 'tank' is right but thin; the table should give the 6-cm depth: the authors expect success to differ in deeper water (prey could escape vertically) and to rise in dim light

claims.claim: esocids attack from inside a school at ~70 % success (Jolles et al. 2022)
claims.source_value: northern pike only (no other esocid was tested), in a 6-cm-deep arena: in 63.2 % of the attacks the pike's head was already partly inside the school's boundary; 70 % is the success over ALL 125 attacks, not of those launched from inside. Pike approached slowly (69 % of attacks at < 0.5 BL/s), mostly head-on, and struck from ~5.3 cm; success fell with the target's distance and its acceleration
claims.location: p. 6 of 26 (PDF p. 6); p. 1 (PDF p. 1), abstract; p. 5 (PDF p. 5)
claims.quote: for more than half the attacks (63.2%), the pike was already partly inside
claims.note: applying a pike-in-a-shallow-tank value to chain pickerel in a lake is the project's extrapolation; say 'pike struck from inside the school in ~63 % of attacks and caught prey on 70 % of all attacks'

notes: Targeted shiners were in relatively central positions (front–back rank 0.45) and far from and less aligned with neighbours; pike targeted the largest groups. The shiners learned to avoid the area in front of the pike's head over repeated exposures, so pike attacked from further away.
